data.narrative:
Krevera is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Edward and Sebastian Schneeweiss that has raised $3M+. The valuation analysis draws on a sector universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), though the private peer set—including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI—lacks sufficient same-stage depth for reliable median pricing.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach. Using the $3M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement, this method implies an $8M post-money valuation. The peer-median approach was not applied; while 11 robotics and manufacturing peers exist in the dataset, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier companies yielded fewer than three datapoints, making sector-wide aggregation unreliably broad.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $6M to $9M, with $8M as the central point. This range reflects ±15% variance around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficient narrowly-filtered comparables to validate or triangulate against the single method employed, and the reliance on total raised as a proxy for last-valuation round in the absence of disclosed post-money terms. Additional diligence on burn rate, product-market fit indicators, and customer traction would strengthen conviction in this range.
